title: The Context Window — July 1, 2026: New Silicon, Open Weights, and Agents That Ship
intro: A dense start to July: cheaper inference silicon, a genuinely open frontier-class model, and agent tooling that is starting to look production-grade. (This is a sample digest — the pipeline replaces it on its first run.)
meta_description: A 3nm inference chip, a frontier-class open-weights release, and agent tooling that finally survives production. Today's 2-minute engineering brief.

stories.headline: Acme ships 3nm inference accelerator claiming 2x performance per watt
stories.what_happened: Acme announced the A100X, a 3nm inference accelerator with 192GB of HBM4 and a claimed 2x performance-per-watt improvement over its previous generation.
stories.why_it_matters: Inference cost dominates LLM serving economics; a 2x efficiency jump directly cuts the price of high-volume production workloads.
stories.outlook: Volume availability is slated for Q4, and cloud partner announcements are expected at the company's developer conference.

stories.headline: OpenLab releases 70B open-weights model under Apache 2.0
stories.what_happened: OpenLab published full weights, the training recipe, and evaluation results for its 70B-parameter model under a permissive Apache 2.0 license.
stories.why_it_matters: Engineers get a commercially usable, frontier-class base model with a documented training pipeline — no research-only license restrictions.
stories.outlook: Community fine-tuned variants are expected within weeks, and the release puts pricing pressure on closed-model APIs.

stories.headline: Agent framework adds deterministic replay for production debugging
stories.what_happened: A widely used agent framework shipped deterministic replay, letting engineers re-run any production agent trajectory locally with identical tool results.
stories.why_it_matters: Non-reproducible failures have been the biggest blocker to debugging agents in production; replay makes them tractable with standard tooling.
stories.outlook: Watch for observability vendors to integrate trajectory replay into their tracing products next.

narration_script: Good morning, it's July first. Three stories today. First, Acme announced a new 3nm inference accelerator...
